item.title: Microchip Nd:YAG laser with master-oscillator–power-amplifier architecture
item.description: Nature Photonics, Published online: 30 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41566-026-01984-2 This work reports an integrated Nd:Y3Al5O12 laser–amplifier system based on a microchip master-oscillator–power-amplifier architecture. A double-resonant microring seed with a 2.9 μW threshold is combined with waveguide amplifiers, enabling continuous-wave output powers exceeding 12 dBm.

item.title: Lightsaber-like plasma antenna uses laser-ionized air to transmit radio waves
item.description: Researchers have demonstrated a technique that uses a laser to produce a plasma beam antenna capable of transmitting radio waves. The article, "Laser-Induced-Plasma-Filament Antenna Transmitting 30 MHz VHF," is published in the IEEE Journal of Microwaves.
item.source: Phys.org 物理新闻

item.title: Protons ride moving waves to reach record energy with long-pulse lasers
item.description: Imagine a proton catching a wave and surfing it to gain speed. While the imagery may seem wild, the premise of laser-driven ion acceleration has promise as an alternative to conventional accelerators. However, the ultrathin targets used to drive this increase in ion energy are vulnerable to the weak prepulse that precedes the main high-intensity laser pulse, meaning an adaptation in the process is necessary.
item.source: Phys.org 物理新闻

item.title: A laser that stays locked without active control
item.description: EPFL researchers have developed a chip-based laser that keeps a very stable frequency across its tested operating range, without needing active electronic control. Their research is published in the journal Nature Photonics.
item.source: Phys.org 物理新闻

item.title: Laser-made muons produce first images of dense objects
item.description: Muons are constantly being created as cosmic rays collide with molecules in Earth's upper atmosphere. With their ability to penetrate far into dense, solid materials, these cosmic muons are often used to image the insides of objects that are otherwise hidden from view. However, the flow of these natural particles is far too slow for the technique to become both fast and reliable in practical settings.
item.source: Phys.org 物理新闻

item.title: Rotating light pattern reveals laser frequency in a single image
item.description: An international team of physicists has developed a new method for determining the precise color of laser light using an image that rotates as the laser's frequency shifts.
item.source: Phys.org 物理新闻
